external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party card processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: It is the only thing exposed to the internet. Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker that processes orders and reads and writes order data.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The password for the database application account comes from an environment variable on the worker. The service uses its own service account for the receipt archive.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)
data_stores.notes: The order service accesses it with a single application account that has full read/write.

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_stores.notes: Each receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: A shopper browses the storefront and places orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for each completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account
data_flows.data_description: receipt recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated." Authentication is therefore unknown.
data_flows.data_description: payment settlement status indicating that the order is paid

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the third-party card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface because shoppers browse the storefront through it.
assumptions.basis: The source describes shoppers browsing the storefront and placing orders through the storefront API.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface because it is a worker reached through gRPC.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the component as a Python worker and states that the storefront API calls it over gRPC.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database contains confidential data because it stores shopper addresses and card-last-four values along with orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in orders-db.
